docs.title: Image Comparator
docs.text:
Image Comparator is an app for checking whether two photos show the same individual animal. It is the manual step of a mostly automated re-identification pipeline:

  1. The animal_re_id package compares new photos (the query) with photos of known individuals (the database) and proposes the most likely pairs.
  2. In Image Comparator, you answer for every proposed pair whether the two animals are the same.
  3. Your answers are used to assign identities to the new photos.

The computer does the time-consuming search through all photos. You only check a few of the most promising candidates, and every identity is confirmed by a human.

docs.title: What the app does for you
docs.text:
• Shows the pairs one by one, ordered from the most promising, together with the body part (for example the head) that produced the match.
  • Skips pairs whose answer is already known from your previous answers.
  • Prevents contradictions between your answers.
  • Saves every answer immediately, so you can close the app at any time and continue later.

docs.title: Custom datasets
docs.text: The provided example downloads everything it needs. To verify your own photos, you describe your dataset in a config file. No coding is needed.

docs.title: Identification and discovery
docs.text:
The app supports two types of tasks:

  • Identification: for projects with an established database, where new photos are matched with known individuals.
  • Discovery: for new projects without an established database, where new photos are matched among themselves.

docs.title: What the app needs
docs.text:
The app uses the files created by animal_re_id, for example in its introduction notebook:

  • Photos: metadata.csv and segmentation.csv created by animal_re_id. The data structure must be the same as the one passed to animal_re_id. The photos are usually in the local data folder, but can be anywhere by using the config below.
  • Pairs: verification_data.csv exported by animal_re_id. Copy it to the folder where the app is started.

The app creates answers.csv in the folder where it is started. Use a separate folder for every dataset.

docs.title: Running the app
docs.text:
The app has two built-in configs, identification and discovery, which read the data from the folder data. The tabs below show the commands for both. Selecting a tab switches all tabs on this page. To start the app, run

IdentificationDiscovery 
image-comparator identification

The folder data contains the folders query and database, each containing metadata.csv and segmentation.csv.

image-comparator discovery

The folder data contains metadata.csv and segmentation.csv.

docs.title: Custom config
docs.text:
If the data are elsewhere, create a config file, for example my_project.json, with the path to the data and run the app with it:

IdentificationDiscovery 
{
  "root": "/path/to/turtle_re_id/examples/data_identification"
}

image-comparator identification --config my_project.json

{
  "root": "/path/to/my/query"
}

image-comparator discovery --config my_project.json

The config file is merged into the built-in config, so it only needs the keys you want to change:

Key Meaning root Folder with the data described in Running the app. A relative path is relative to the folder where the app is started. Default data. url Optional. Link to a zip file with the content of root, downloaded by --download. downloads Optional. Files downloaded by --download and --download-files, as {"path": "link"}.

docs.title: Sharing a dataset with annotators
docs.text:
If other people verify the pairs, upload the data and let the app download them:

IdentificationDiscovery
  1. Zip the folders query and database into one file and upload it.
  2. Upload verification_data.csv.
  3. Send the annotators the config file with both links:
{
  "url": "https://example.org/my_project/data.zip",
  "downloads": {
    "verification_data.csv": "https://example.org/my_project/verification_data.csv"
  }
}

The annotators save the config file in an empty folder and run there

image-comparator identification --config my_project.json --download

Warning

The option --download downloads the data, which may take a long time. Use it only the first time. Next time, run in the same folder only

image-comparator identification --config my_project.json
  1. Zip metadata.csv, segmentation.csv and the photos into one file and upload it.
  2. Upload verification_data.csv.
  3. Send the annotators the config file with both links:
{
  "url": "https://example.org/my_project/data.zip",
  "downloads": {
    "verification_data.csv": "https://example.org/my_project/verification_data.csv"
  }
}

The annotators save the config file in an empty folder and run there

image-comparator discovery --config my_project.json --download

Warning

The option --download downloads the data, which may take a long time. Use it only the first time. Next time, run in the same folder only

image-comparator discovery --config my_project.json

The zip file is extracted into root. Therefore, the files and folders must be at the top level of the zip file, not inside another folder. The paths in metadata.csv must be relative and the photos must be inside the zip file, otherwise the annotators cannot find them.

When you prepare new pairs, upload the new verification_data.csv to the same link. The annotators move their old answers.csv away and run the app with --download-files instead of --download, which downloads only verification_data.csv and skips the slow download of the photos.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
All commands below are run in a terminal, a text window where commands are typed. To open it:

  • Windows: press the Windows key, type cmd or powershell and press Enter.
  • Mac: press Cmd+Space, type terminal and press Enter.
  • Linux: press Ctrl+Alt+T.

Paste each command into the terminal and press Enter.

docs.title: Step 1: Install Git and uv
docs.text:
uv is a tool for installing Python apps. Run the commands for your system.

WindowsMacLinux (Debian/Ubuntu) 
winget install --id Git.Git -e
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

xcode-select --install
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

sudo apt install git
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

docs.title: Step 2: Install the app
docs.text:
Close the terminal and open a new one. Then run the following command, which is the same for all systems:

uv tool install git+https://github.com/sadda/image-comparator

docs.title: Updating the app
docs.text:
Open a terminal and run

uv tool install --reinstall git+https://github.com/sadda/image-comparator

In case of problems, contact us.

docs.title: Starting the app
docs.text:
The app stores the photos and your answers in the folder where it is started. Therefore, first create a folder for your project and move into it. To try the app on a small example, run

mkdir example_identification
cd example_identification
image-comparator example_identification --download

This downloads a small subset of SeaTurtleID2022 with 6 query encounters and 4 turtles in the database. Four of the query turtles are in the database. The remaining two are new individuals, so all their pairs should be answered Different. To check your answers, the true identities of the query encounters are:

Encounter Identity 2016-09-11/1 new individual 2018-06-22/1 t217 2019-09-01/1 new individual 2019-09-02/1 t023 2021-06-22/1 t243 2021-06-27/1 t441

The first 4 pairs are wrong matches, because they show a new individual. Next time, run only

cd example_identification
image-comparator example_identification

Warning

Always start the app from the same folder, otherwise it will not find your photos and answers. The app refuses to start in your home folder.

docs.title: Example for discovery
docs.text:
The second example compares 10 encounters with each other instead of with a database

mkdir example_discovery
cd example_discovery
image-comparator example_discovery --download

The 10 encounters show 6 turtles. Four turtles were seen twice: 2018-06-22/1 and 2018-08-22/1, 2019-09-01/1 and 2019-09-02/1, 2019-09-01/2 and 2021-06-22/1, and 2019-09-04/1 and 2021-06-27/1. All other pairs should be answered Different.

docs.title: Answering the pairs
docs.text:
The app shows a pair of photos: a query encounter on the left and a candidate on the right. An encounter is a group of photos of one animal taken at one occasion, for example on one day. The title shows the number of the pair and the similarity (the number of matched keypoints). Decide whether the two photos show the same individual.

Button Key Meaning Same Q The two photos show the same individual. Different W The two photos show different individuals. Unknown E You cannot decide. The pair stays unanswered. Previous A Go back to the previous pair, for example to change an answer. Next S Go to the next pair without answering. Next encounter / Next body part – Jump to the first unanswered pair of the next encounter or body part. Toggle heads left / right R / F Show other head photos of the left or right individual. Reset V Show the original pair again.

Tip

Use the keyboard shortcuts Q, W, E, A and S. They make the verification much faster.

Tip

Answer Unknown if you are not sure. An unanswered pair is better than a wrong answer.

Pairs whose answer already follows from your previous answers are skipped automatically. For example, once an encounter was answered Same, its remaining candidates are not shown. If an answer would contradict your previous answers, it is not accepted and a message is shown. To change it, go back and change the previous answer.

docs.title: Your answers
docs.text:
The answers are saved after every click to answers.csv in the folder where the app is started. You can close the app at any time and continue later from where you left off. The file contains all proposed pairs with two additional columns:

Column Content answer same, different, or empty for unanswered pairs time Seconds spent on the pair

Send this file back to the person who prepared the verification.

Warning

answers.csv belongs to one verification_data.csv. When you receive new pairs (--download-files), first move the old answers.csv to another folder or rename it. Otherwise the app reports that answers.csv has wrong format and closes.
